newsitem.title: ITALY: Haiti holds talks to try to appease banana growers.
newsitem.headline: Haiti holds talks to try to appease banana growers.

text.p: Haiti's Agriculture Minister Gerald Mathurin said on Friday he had held talks with his counterpart from the Dominican Republic to try to appease Haitian banana producers who feel threatened by imports from their neighbours.
"We've been under quite a lot of pressure from Haitian banana producers who believe the government should intervene," Mathurin told Reuters on the margins of a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit.
"So I have talked with my Dominican colleague (Nicolas Concepion Garcia). He is here. We have held discussions...to try to find a solution."
He said the Dominican Republic exported bananas at lower prices, causing a slow in sales of Haiti produce. He declined to give figures for Haiti's banana production.

Mathurin said government subsidies were not necessarily being considered. "There are no solutions yet. We must consider the situation together (with the Dominican Republic) and see what the possible solutions are," he said.
"I think the producers are calling above all for a regulated trade in line with the general norms of international trade," he said. "I hope some progress will be made soon."
